A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MnI‐catalyized C−H activation is a powerful tool for the construction of new bonds and the formation of complex molecules, which is a promising strategy for the development of novel synthetic methods.

we have developed a new catalytic method for C−H bond functionalization that is enabled by the unique reactivity of a highly reactive 7‐membered Mn‐acyclic complex, which is formed in situ by the combination of a manganese(I) precursor and a 2‐arylpyridine substrate.

the 2‐pyryl group can be used as a versatile directing group to activate the C−H bonds adjacent to the carbonyl group, which can undergo a wide range of transformations, such as the C−H bond functionalization, C−H bond cleavage, and C−H activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 7‐membered Mn‐cycle is a key intermediate in the H‐transfer or the reductive elimination pathways.
a seven‐membered manganese complex is a key intermediate for both H‐transfer and reductive elimination pathways in MnI‐catalyed C−H bond functionalization.
the MnI‐intermediate can be used as an effective platform for C−H functionalization, which has been underexplored to date.
